_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: An MCP tool's view renders and works with the conversation. The MCP server "counter" has the tool show_counter, whose view shows a counter, the app-only tool increment, and the tool leave, whose view goes to another page before it loads. The agent has run, in the conversation /c/{{SLUG}}, "shelley mcp call counter.show_counter start=1" and then "shelley mcp call counter.leave". Each call's view shows in the conversation in a card (data-testid "message-mcpapp") as an iframe titled with the call's name: "the view" is the frame "iframe[title='counter.show_counter']", and "the left view" the frame "iframe[title='counter.leave']". The view's elements are #count, #input, #theme, #background, #mode, #connect, #eval, #worker and #worker-connect, and the buttons #increment, #tell, #fullscreen and #leave; its scripts define window.tell(text) (asks the host to send text as the user's message), window.handOn() (hands every port the view holds to another one) and window.overheard (what reached the ports handed on). The page a view goes to has #sent. "The card" is the data-testid "message-mcpapp" whose text contains "counter.show_counter", and "the frame" its data-testid "mcp-app-frame". Call "agent told" says whether the agent was told the user sees the result in an interactive view ("true" or "false"). Name elements by ARIA role and accessible name, as Playwright's getByRole does; "named X" means an exact name match. "The consent bar" is data-testid "mcp-app-consent", where the host asks the user's OK for what a view asks to do. To "send T": fill data-testid "message-input" with T and click data-testid "send-button". "The agent says T": the last ".message-agent" whose text contains T should be visible (timeout 30s). Perform the steps in order. 1. Call "agent told": it must return "true". 2. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}. The view that left before loading shows the page it went to: the left view's #sent should have exactly the text "sent". 3. The call's input and result, and the host's theme: the view's #count should have exactly the text "Counter at 1", its #input "start=1" and its #theme "theme light". Eval, in the page, getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--bg-base").trim(), saving it as BG: the view's #background should have exactly the text {{BG}}. Its #mode should have exactly the text "mode inline". The view loads its script from its resourceDomains, and nothing else: its #connect should have exactly the text "blocked", #eval "eval ok", #worker "worker ok" and #worker-connect "blocked". 4. An app-only tool, and context the model gets with the next message: click the view's #increment; its #count should have exactly the text "Counter at 2". Send "app context?". The agent says '<view_context source="counter.show_counter"', and the agent says "The counter shows 2". The data-testid "message-app-context" whose text contains "counter.show_counter" should be visible. 5. Taken once: send "app context?"; the agent says "no app context". 6. A message from the view, which the user allows: click the view's #tell. The consent bar should contain the text "counter.show_counter asks to send" and the text "echo: counter at 2". Click the consent bar's button named "Send". The ".message-user" whose text contains "echo: counter at 2" should be visible, and there should be no consent bar (count 0). 7. Or doesn't: eval, in the view, window.unasked = window.tell("echo: unasked").then((result) => JSON.stringify(result)); "asked". The consent bar should contain the text "echo: unasked". 8. Another request can't take its place: eval, in the view, window.swapped = window.tell("echo: swapped").then(JSON.stringify, (err) => err.message); "asked". Then eval, in the view, window.swapped.then((t) => t.includes("waiting for the user") ? "refused" : t) until it returns "refused". The consent bar should still contain the text "echo: unasked". 9. Click the consent bar's button named "Cancel". Eval, in the view, window.unasked.then((t) => t.includes('"isError":true') ? "cancelled" : t) until it returns "cancelled". There should be no consent bar (count 0). 10. Fullscreen, and back: click the view's #fullscreen. The frame should have the attribute data-display-mode exactly "fullscreen", and the view's #mode exactly the text "mode fullscreen". Click the frame's button named "Close". The frame should have the attribute data-display-mode exactly "inline", and the view's #mode exactly the text "mode inline". 11. The theme follows Shelley's: emulate prefers-color-scheme: dark. The view's #theme should have exactly the text "theme dark". Eval, in the page, getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--bg-base").trim() again, saving it as DARK. Eval "{{DARK}}" === "{{BG}}": it must return false. The view's #background should have exactly the text {{DARK}}. 12. Ports the view hands on don't reach the host (and handing on its own ends what it hears from the host): eval, in the view, window.handOn(). What the host says next goes past the view, but tells them nothing: emulate prefers-color-scheme: light, then eval, in the view, window.overheard.length ? JSON.stringify(window.overheard.filter((m) => m !== "null")) : "none yet" until it returns "[]". 13. Nor does a page the view goes to: click the view's #leave; the view's #sent should have exactly the text "sent". Send "app context?". There should be exactly 2 ".message-agent" whose text contains "no app context" (timeout 30s). There should be no ".message-user" whose text contains "unasked" (count 0), no ".message-agent" whose text contains "elsewhere" (count 0), and no ".message-agent" whose text contains "handed on" (count 0).

steps.expression: window.swapped.then((t) => t.includes('waiting for the user') ? 'refused' : t)
